Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WARABIMOCHI IS ONE OF THE BEST JAPANESE SWEETS FOR BOTH DIETS AND IT DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON A WORD THE SHOP DOES NOT USE. True warabimochi is set from 本蕨粉 — BRACKEN ROOT STARCH — which is a fern rhizome: no wheat, no dairy, no egg, nothing animal, and it is dusted with きな粉 (roasted SOYBEAN flour) and eaten with 黒蜜 (cane syrup). On that construction it is plant and gluten-free outright. ⚠ BUT ALMOST NO COMMERCIAL WARABIMOCHI IS MADE THAT WAY. Bracken starch is scarce and expensive, so the overwhelming majority of shops use a blend of sweet-potato or tapioca starch — still wheat-free — and some use わらび餅粉 blends that include other starches. The shop says only 「原料、製法にこだわって作られる」, that it is particular about materials and method, which is a quality claim and not an ingredient one. It does not name 本蕨粉 anywhere. So the base is very likely wheat-free but is not declared, which is why these are "ask" rather than "gf". ⚠ AND THE DRINKS ARE THE OPPOSITE WAY ROUND: わらび餅ミルクティー and わらび餅ソフトクリーム are both DAIRY — the mochi is the plant part and the vehicle is not. The soft serve is Asakusa-only.

items.note: ⚠ THE BASE IS ALMOST CERTAINLY WHEAT-FREE AND IS NOT DECLARED. Warabimochi is set from bracken-root or other root starch — never wheat — and dusted with きな粉, roasted soybean flour. Both flags stay open because the shop names neither its starch nor whether the kinako or syrup carry anything else. If the answer comes back 本蕨粉, きな粉 and 黒蜜, this is a dessert that clears both diets.
The brown-sugar version. 黒糖 is unrefined cane sugar — plant.
Matcha is powdered green tea, plant and wheat-free in itself.
